# The Delegation Divide — Agent Delegability Index (ADI)

> Open index of AI-agent delegability for 433 ISCO-08 occupations and 146 countries (v2026.1).
> Headline: 35.2% of task time in world employment is at least partly delegable to AI agents (L2+) in 2026;
> only 2.5% can be handed over in full (L3). 48.7% in high-income vs 22.5% in low-income countries
> (the "delegation divide": +7.23 pp per log point of GDP per capita). Full delegation peaks for tasks
> that take a human about twelve minutes. Source of every number: salidas/claims.jsonl.
> Four levels per task: L0 no role, L1 augmentation, L2 partial delegation, L3 full delegation.
> Rated by Claude Sonnet 5.5 and Claude Haiku 5.5 on 18,796 O*NET 30.2 tasks; human validation in progress.
> Preregistered at OSF: https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/9ZNTF · Data and code: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23552918

## How to use
- Occupation lookup (static JSON): release/v2026.1/api/isco/<4-digit ISCO-08>.json (e.g. isco/2512.json)
- Country lookup (static JSON): release/v2026.1/api/country/<ISO3>.json (e.g. country/COL.json); index: release/v2026.1/api/index.json
- Tables: release/v2026.1/adi_isco.csv, adi_pais.csv, adi_tarea.csv (+ .parquet); columns in release/v2026.1/DATA_DICTIONARY.md
- MCP server: adi-mcp (tools: lookup_occupation, country_profile, top_occupations, cite)
- Python: pip install adi-index

## How to cite
See CITATION.cff. BibTeX key: espinal2026delegation. Every JSON record carries a `cite` field.

## Files
- README.md: BibTeX, headline block, summary
- llms-full.txt: definitions, column schema, tool reference
- docs/PLAN.md: full design
- salidas/claims.jsonl: every number in the paper (public copy: release/v2026.1/claims.jsonl)
